cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Rate limiting caps how many requests a client can make in a time window so one caller cannot overload a shared service or run up costs. Autoscaling alone does not help because it lags and shared dependencies do not scale with it.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: A token bucket allows bursts but enforces an average; enforce at the API gateway per API key with a shared Redis counter updated atomically (for example a Lua script). Rejections get 429 with Retry-After. Fixed windows allow about 2 times the limit at boundaries; sliding windows fix that.

questions.q: A customer limited to 100 per minute gets about 400. Why?
questions.a: Likely four instances each enforcing 100 with local counters. Use a shared atomic counter.
Token bucket for inbound limits, allowing bursts. Leaky bucket for smoothing outbound calls to a fragile downstream.

questions.q: A whole university gets 429s while barely using the API. Why?
questions.a: The limit is keyed by IP and thousands share one NAT address. Key on user or API key.
